title: Aurora color seams — OKLCh catch-light + the shared palette-ramp twin
headline: Close the two OKLCh seam leaks the W5 migration missed: (1) OKLCh-derive aurora's warm-white catch-light off a shared warmCatchLight(L,C,h) /color helper (delete the eyeballed [1.0,0.95,0.88] literal); (2) HOIST the palette-ramp interpolation (smoothstep ease + huePath OKLab-rect-vs-OKLCh-hue-arc dispatch) into the shared procedural-color chunk as PALETTE_RAMP_GLSL/PALETTE_RAMP_WGSL twins both samplePalette ports splice — closing the W07 WGSL samplePalette gate hole (the flat-lerp-rainbow drift). Plus the planned->landed README/DESIGN sweep keyed off the registered gates. SEAM-LEVEL, NOT a migration redo (S4 note 7: the OKLCh core is genuinely landed).

liveRediagnosis.ritual: AX.W00 wave-open — code-level re-diagnosis confirmed at HEAD e32d944 before any edit; all three RED witnesses re-proven, not taken on the audit's word.

witness1_wgsl_samplePalette_incomplete_t.claim: The WGSL samplePalette (aurora.wgsl.ts:140-152) does a plain oklabToLinearSrgb(mix(labA,labB,f)) with NO smoothstep ease and NO huePath branch — no huePath uniform at all. The GLSL samplePalette (composition.glsl.ts) smoothstep-eases + dispatches mixPaletteOklab/mixPaletteOklchArc on uHuePath. So a WebGPU huePath:'increasing' rainbow config silently flat-lerps; proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence certifies ONLY the OETF/matrices/FBM chunk, NOT samplePalette — the gate hole.
witness1_wgsl_samplePalette_incomplete_t.numericEvidence: Reconstructed HEAD flat-lerp vs the GLSL oracle's smoothstep+arc ramp on a distant-hue (blue->yellow) linear stop pair at t in {0.25,0.5,0.75}: flat(smoothstep) path |delta| = 1.262e-1 (the missing ease); arc(huePath) path |delta| = 5.704e-1 (the entire missing hue-arc) — both >> 1e-6 (RED on BOTH huePath paths).
witness1_wgsl_samplePalette_incomplete_t.structuralEvidence: git show e32d944:aurora.wgsl.ts — PALETTE_RAMP_WGSL splice absent, samplePaletteRamp call absent, `oklabToLinearSrgb(mix(labA, labB, f))` flat-lerp present, `huePath: f32` struct field absent; procedural-color.glsl.ts — PALETTE_RAMP_GLSL export absent.

witness2_catchlight_srgb_literal.claim: Aurora's lightColor default was the raw RGB literal [1.0, 0.95, 0.88] (uniformBridge.ts:324) declared 'warm-white tint (linear)', fed to mediums/brush impasto as a linear multiplier with NO OKLCh derivation — while the blob's warmCream IS OKLCh-derived (metaball.frag.ts:359 oklabToLinearSrgb(oklchToOklab(vec3(0.97,0.03,radians(85.0))))).
witness2_catchlight_srgb_literal.grepEvidence: grep '1.0, 0.95, 0.88' uniformBridge.ts = 1 hit; grep 'warmCatchLight' src/composables/color/index.ts = 0 (no shared OKLCh catch-light helper existed).

folds.finding: slice 7 F3 (major root) — the WGSL samplePalette is an incomplete color twin; the gate has a hole
folds.rootCause: The W5 palette-ramp interpolation (smoothstep ease + huePath OKLab-rect-vs-OKLCh-hue-arc dispatch) lived inline in aurora.frag.ts; the WGSL twin (aurora.wgsl.ts, AW.W7b) was a hand-transcribed flat OKLab lerp that never carried the ease or the hue-arc. The matrices-only proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence could not see the ramp drift.
folds.gestaltFix: HOISTED interpolateHueTurns + mixPaletteOklab + mixPaletteOklchArc + a new smoothstep-eased samplePaletteRamp(a,b,tRaw,huePath) dispatcher into procedural-color.glsl.ts as GLSL+WGSL twins (PALETTE_RAMP_GLSL / PALETTE_RAMP_WGSL), the SAME two-copy-elimination pattern AV.W1 established for the OETF. Both samplePalette ports now SPLICE the shared ramp: composition.glsl.ts selects the bracketing stop pair + raw t -> samplePaletteRamp; aurora.wgsl.ts does the same on the storage-Field index + carries a huePath:f32 uniform (i32-cast in-shader). The ramp can NEVER drift between backends.
folds.evidence: procedural-color.glsl.ts (+PALETTE_RAMP_GLSL @:147, +PALETTE_RAMP_WGSL); aurora.frag.ts (inline 3 fns removed, ${PALETTE_RAMP_GLSL} spliced); composition.glsl.ts samplePalette -> samplePaletteRamp; aurora.wgsl.ts samplePalette splices ${PALETTE_RAMP_WGSL}+samplePaletteRamp, struct Uniforms +huePath:f32; uniformBridge.ts packGPUUniforms writes huePath @slot16, WGPU_UNIFORM_FLOATS 16->20 (vec4-aligned).

catchLightAnchor.decision: AURORA_CATCH_LIGHT_ANCHOR = {L:0.985, C:0.0125, h:77.5}. The spec demanded the helper reproduce BOTH the prior [1.0,0.95,0.88] warm-white AND the blob's warmCream (0.97,0.03,85) anchor — but those two land at DIFFERENT linear triples ([1.0,0.95,0.88] vs [0.9955,0.9055,0.7371]; the blob cream is ~0.14 bluer-deficient). The VISUAL-TRUTH binding constraint ('the aurora relight reads the SAME warm-white, no visible shift') is the dominant one, so the aurora anchor reproduces the prior literal (<1e-3 linear). The CROSS-SURFACE UNIFICATION is the shared DERIVATION (one warmCatchLight helper), not one hardcoded anchor: aurora passes its anchor, W15's blob passes (0.97,0.03,85). The helper is parameterized warmCatchLight(L,C,hDeg) for exactly this. RATIFIED in-wave per the spec's derivation rule ('pick the anchor that lands the same perceptual warm-white').

w15WarmCreamOrdering.decision: W11 does NOT touch metaball.frag.ts (the blob warmCream re-route is W15). W11 only READS :359 as the OKLCh anchor reference + proves warmCatchLight(0.97,0.03,85) is byte-identical to oklchToLinear({L:0.97,C:0.03,h:85}) (the test asserts delta==0), so W15 inherits a true drop-in.
